title: Derive strategic tiers from project configuration
description:
Implement the pre-flight logic that derives jit-project-lead's steward anchor (the most-strategic type) and delegation boundary (the container types it dispatches an execution lead for) purely from each project's own configuration, with an explicit stop-and-ask fallback when the configuration is ambiguous or missing.

## Background

jit backs software projects (this repo, hierarchy `milestone` > `epic`) and non-software ones (a research example where `strategic_types = ["goal"]` and `goal` is itself the breakable container, collapsing to a single strategic tier). The steward anchor is the first entry of `strategic_types` in `.jit/config.toml`; the delegation boundary is the union of `applies_to` across `[[template]]` entries in `.jit/templates.toml`. When `templates.toml` is missing or `strategic_types` is empty, the logic falls back to the numeric type-to-level map returned by `jit config show-hierarchy --json`. The logic must be expressed with zero hardcoded domain type literals (no `milestone`, `epic`, or `goal` string in its control-flow) so it works unmodified against any project's ruleset.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Running the derivation against this repository's `.jit/config.toml` and `.jit/templates.toml` yields `milestone` as the steward anchor and `epic` as the delegation boundary.
- [hard] REQ-02: Running the derivation against `docs/examples/research/config.toml` (`strategic_types = ["goal"]`) and `docs/examples/research/templates.toml` (`applies_to = ["goal"]`) yields the collapsed case: a single strategic tier, with `goal` as both the steward anchor and the delegation boundary.
- [hard] REQ-03: When `.jit/templates.toml` is missing, when `strategic_types` is empty, or when the derivation would leave a genuine level tie among candidate anchors, the logic stops and reports the ambiguity instead of guessing an anchor or boundary.
- [hard] REQ-04: When `.jit/templates.toml` is missing or `strategic_types` is empty, the logic falls back to reading the type-to-level map from `jit config show-hierarchy --json` before giving up.
- [hard] REQ-05: No string literal `milestone`, `epic`, or `goal` appears anywhere in the derivation's control-flow logic; type names are read only from configuration.
- [hard] REQ-06: After the derivation logic is added, `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/SKILL.md` remains under 500 lines; if authoring it directly in `SKILL.md` would exceed budget, it is extracted into a `references/` file read on demand with only a routing stub left in `SKILL.md`.

## Notes

This logic lives in jit-project-lead's pre-flight step, authored inline in `SKILL.md` or in a `references/` file it reads on demand. Skill prose follows the cc-sdd/superpowers register (terse imperative voice, explicit stop-and-escalate conditions, red-flag lists over prose warnings); consult `../jit-research/cc-sdd/tools/cc-sdd/templates/agents/claude-code-skills/skills/kiro-spec-design/SKILL.md`, `../jit-research/superpowers/skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md`, and `../jit-research/superpowers/skills/executing-plans/SKILL.md` as exemplars. Prose refers to "strategic tier" / "sub-strategic tier" as placeholders, never literal type names, matching the `<planning_type>`/`<breakdown_type>` convention already used by `jit-execution-lead`.
